results.content: version. They all record, transcribe and summarise. None is meaningfully better at that than the others, and most cost US$8–18 a month but here's what actually separates them 👇 1. Otter 💴 Free: 300 mins a month, 30 min max per convo and only 25 most recent kept 💴 Paid: US$8.33/mo billed yearly 💼 Solid bot-free option, but the free tier won't cut it for long client meetings. Also seen billing complaints on App Store, including a Singapore user charged on day one of a "free trial". 2. Granola 💴 Free: Keeps only 30 days of meeting history. 💴 Paid: US$14/mo 💼 What I personally use for online meetings and it's been great! Accurate, reliable and great UI (The free tier is enough for most but if you want MCP, you would need to upgrade) 3. Fathom 💴 Free: Unlimited recording, transcription and [...] past transcripts into actual meeting insights. 6. tl;dv Read.ai 💴 Free: 5 transcripts a month with a 1-hour cap 💴 Paid: US$15/month yearly 💼 Haven't actually tried this yet, but it looks promising! People are raving about its in-person recording being good and it has an assistant who goes past transcripts into actual meeting insights. 6. tl;dv 💴 Free: 10 meetings with AI notes, unlimited mobile recording and 3-month retention. 💴 Paid: US$18/month billed yearly 💼 Another one that I haven't tried, but on paper, the best offline recorder here because it can run up to 3 hours with no signal. However, all six of its App Store reviews are one or two stars, mostly about recordings that vanished. A quick note on all of them is that none of them: → keep a contacts book that builds context on every [...] a meeting because it kills the conversation. So he drops two-word fragments into Telegram Saved Messages, and then expands them into real notes on the commute home which would live on Notion and Obsidian (Cool!) 5. Self-service Honestly, why didn't we think of this? This advisor sends clients a Google Form and have them self-report their own preferences and wishes.
